title: Preemptible Credit Pools for Dedicated Capacity — PRD
creator: Aisha Kwon
description: Introduce a first-class preemptible credit pool capability for Dedicated capacity customers. This PRD defines a mechanism where tenants can consume lower-priority (preemptible) spare capacity using a credit accounting system that enables predictable cost savings, graceful eviction, and clear telemetry for billing and troubleshooting.
problem_statement: Some Dedicated customers want lower-cost burst throughput and are willing to accept best-effort preemptible execution. Today we lack a formal, auditable credit model or control plane UX to offer preemptible capacity tied to reserved Dedicated pools. That gap prevents offering a priced product tier with predictable economics and safe eviction semantics.
goals: Define credit accounting and lifetime semantics for preemptible capacity
Provide runtime admission and eviction rules that preserve critical reserved capacity SLOs
Expose console and API controls for purchasing/allocating credits and observing usage
Ship clear acceptance criteria, telemetry, and billing integration so customers can reconcile charges
non_goals: Replace existing Dedicated reservation primitives (no change to core reservation API)
Support unbounded multi-tenant leasing of GPU nodes (scope is per-tenant pool attachments only)
Provide deep workload-level QoS (e.g., per-request priority beyond credit accounting) in this phase
success_metrics: 20% of pilot tenants opt into preemptible credits in first 8 weeks
Average cost-per-token for preemptible runs is >= 30% lower than reserved baseline
No P0 incidents caused by preemptible eviction during gated pilot
Telemetry accuracy: <1% mismatch between runtime credit consumption and billing ledger after reconciliation
user_stories: As an engineering lead, I want to buy a credit package and map it to my dedicated pool so burst traffic uses preemptible capacity when available
As an SRE, I want clear eviction logs and tenant attribution when preemptible workloads are preempted
As a finance contact, I want usage export that ties consumed credits to invoice line items
scope: Credit ledger service to track per-tenant credit balances (add/deduct, refund flows)
Runtime admission hooks to allow preemptible tasks when headroom exists and to evict them based on credit exhaustion and SLO preemption rules
Console UI: purchase flow for credit bundles, view of current balance and recent consumption
API: endpoints to query balance, attach credit pool to Dedicated reservation, and trigger refunds
Billing: add invoice line for consumed preemptible credits and reconcile with ledger events
Observability: events and dashboards for consumed credits, preemptions, offtarget SLO impacts
out_of_scope: Sophisticated marketplace pricing or secondary market for credits
requirements: R1: Credit unit semantics — 1 credit = 1 preemptible-second of equivalent rX throughput (documented conversion table)
R2: Runtime must check tenant credit balance atomically before admitting preemptible request sequence and deduct credits as tokens emitted
R3: Eviction policy must prioritize preserving reserved capacity SLOs: reserved requests never evicted for preemptible credits
R4: Refund window — customers can request refund of unused credits within 30 days of purchase
R5: Console UX — purchase button, bundle options (small/medium/large), and consumption timeline visualization
R6: Telemetry — emitted events: credit_acquired, credit_consumed, credit_refunded, preemptible_admitted, preemptible_evicted
R7: Billing export — daily CSV of tenant credit consumption for invoice reconciliation
api_changes: GET /v1/dedicated/{pool_id}/credits -> current balance and last 30 transactions
POST /v1/dedicated/{pool_id}/credits/attach -> attach a purchased bundle to a pool
console_changes: New Credits tab under Dedicated Pool detail: purchase bundles, attach/detach bundles, view balance
Consumption chart with per-hour granularity and markers for preemptions
Admin modal to issue manual refunds and view pending refund requests
runtime_changes: Admission hook that calls ledger service to verify/deduct credit before accepting a preemptible request
Eviction engine integration: mark preemptible tasks with eviction metadata and emit preemptible_evicted events
Backoff policy: when credit balance < threshold, stop admitting new preemptible work and surface to console
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Pilot tenants can purchase a credit bundle via console and see an accurate ledger entry
AC-2: Preemptible admission only occurs when pool headroom > configured safety buffer and tenant has positive credits
AC-3: When credits are exhausted mid-request, runtime finishes the token currently in-flight and subsequently rejects new preemptible admissions; eviction events include transaction id and reason
AC-4: Billing CSV matches runtime-ledger consumption for pilot tenants within 1% discrepancy for sample week
AC-5: No reserved-pool SLO regression detected during 2-week pilot (latency/throughput within existing SLOs)
AC-6: Console shows consumption timeline that correlates to telemetry events (credit_consumed, preemptible_evicted)
AC-7: Refund flow executes and updates ledger and billing in less than 72 hours
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (engineering alpha): internal only, ledger + runtime hooks + unit tests
Phase 1 (gated pilot): invite 5 existing Dedicated customers, manual refunds and SRE oncall
Phase 2 (beta): open to self-serve purchase for select accounts, add automated refunds, billing exports
Phase 3 (general availability): public docs, pricing SKU, full console automation and SLA language
monitoring_and_alerts: Dashboards: credit supply by tenant, admission rate, eviction rate, headroom utilization
Alerts: spike in preemptible_evicted events (>5/min across cluster), ledger mismatch (>2% daily), failed purchase transactions (>0.5% of buys)
SLO guard: auto-disable preemptible admission cluster-wide if reserved latency SLO breaches for 10 consecutive minutes
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Evictions could inadvertently impact reserved SLOs. Mitigation: conservative safety buffer and hard guard to never evict reserved work.
Risk: Billing reconciliation drift between ledger and runtime. Mitigation: event-based CDC stream + daily reconciliation job and alerting.
Risk: Abuse (tenants trying to bypass reservations). Mitigation: rate limits on attach API and audit logs surfaced in console.
dependencies: ENG-90234: Eviction engine telemetry hooks and metadata propagation
ENG-91500: Billing export pipeline changes to accept credit consumption line items
DES-12045: Console UI patterns for purchases and timeline charts
open_questions: Q1: Conversion rate — how many credits per GPU-second for each supported instance shape? (requires benchmarking)
Q2: Pricing tiers — should we discount committed customers differently than new customers?
Q3: Refund policy edge cases — what happens to partially consumed credits from a bundle?
Q4: Should preemptible credits be transferable between pools owned by same tenant? (out of scope for v1)
decisions: D1: Use a centralized ledger service (single source of truth) rather than local caches for v1 to avoid reconciliation drift
D2: Do not allow preemptible admission to cause preemption of any request marked as reserved or pinned
D3: Expose purchase bundles only in the Console for pilot; API purchase will be added in beta
security_considerations: Audit logs for all purchase/refund/attach operations must be written to KMS-backed audit store
RBAC: only pool owners and billing admins may initiate refunds or attach bundles
Ensure ledger endpoints require mutual TLS from internal services
notes_for_engineering: Provide a deterministic idempotency token for purchase API so retried requests do not double-charge
Design ledger transactions to include metadata: tenant_id, pool_id, sku, bundle_id, tx_id
Emit high-cardinality debug logs behind a feature flag for first 2 pilot tenants only
next_steps: Finalize credit-to-GPU conversion table (action: Performance team)
ENG: implement minimal ledger with idempotent purchase flow
DES: produce mockups for Console Credits tab
Schedule pilot kickoff with 3 anchor tenants and support SRE oncall
